headline: Some investors are doubting Firmus, an Australian data centre company whose value has nearly tripled in under two months, ahead of its $5 billion stock market debut.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a notable AI-related listing, but a follow-up with the outcome still to come.
importance_line: It shows investors split over whether AI data centre valuations are running ahead of results, which matters to people whose funds may buy in, but the company's forecast of about $5 billion in yearly earnings within five years is its own estimate and the listing has not yet happened.
summary: Reuters reports that Firmus, an Australian data centre company backed by Blackstone and Nvidia, has a term sheet pricing its shares to value it at about $30.6 billion, nearly triple its August value, and some investors question the jump, citing an "unproven" track record. New since yesterday's report of the valuation target: investors are divided, but early indicative orders already exceed the $5 billion deal size, with investor ordering due to open on Tuesday and trading expected from 23 October.
notes: Follow-up of the 2 Oct edition item C07-05 (Bloomberg, Firmus eyes $30 billion valuation). Reuters page blocked (401); text read from TradingView's republication of the Reuters wire copy. Brief conflict: the brief says to credit the other outlet when the original is blocked, but this is Reuters' own text and Full Report rule 6 says to credit and link the original article, so Reuters and its URL are credited.
